provenance.sourceText: Po przesłaniu pliku faktury do KSeF nie jest możliwe jej edytowanie… Jedyną formą poprawienia błędu… jest wystawienie faktury korygującej w KSeF.

rules.notes: REUSES the citation already read by correction-routes/data/pl.json (route INTERNAL_CREDIT_NOTE, forbidden) — Podręcznik KSeF 2.0 cz. II, § 1.6.2, checked on 2026-08-29 (date preserved as-is: reused, not re-verified by this task). Literal translation from the Polish: « Once the invoice file has been transmitted to KSeF, it is no longer possible to edit it… The ONLY way to correct an error… is to issue a corrective invoice in KSeF. » This is THE most explicit citation among the five new countries on exactly this fact: a Polish invoice transmitted to KSeF is LITERALLY non-editable — correction must go through a separate corrective invoice (faktura korygująca, art. 106j ust. 1 ustawy o VAT), never through a new draft save on the same document. The `statuses: ["draft"]` field applies this principle by refusing to re-save as draft an invoice already 'sent'.

Several Polish accounting-practice sources describe annual-reset invoice numbering as common and accepted, but none is the primary legal text or on-point administrative ruling this catalog's `legal` provenance requires. No source found forbids it either. Stays `never` under issue #515's own rule ("if a country's source does not allow it, or you cannot read it first-hand, that country stays never"). provenance.sourceText: «Art. 106e. 1. Faktura powinna zawierać: [...] 4) numer, za pomocą którego podatnik jest zidentyfikowany na potrzeby podatku, z zastrzeżeniem pkt 24 lit. a oraz pkt 25;»

schemes.notes: Ustawa z dnia 11 marca 2004 r. o podatku od towarów i usług, art. 106e ust. 1 pkt 4 — read as the official consolidated text (tekst jednolity) at Dz.U. 2025 poz. 775 (Obwieszczenie Marszałka Sejmu RP z dnia 21 maja 2025 r.), fetched directly as a PDF from dziennikustaw.gov.pl (https://dziennikustaw.gov.pl/D2025000077501.pdf, landing page https://dziennikustaw.gov.pl/DU/rok/2025/pozycja/775), curl then `pdftotext -layout`, 2026-09-13 — isap.sejm.gov.pl was not used (sits behind Incapsula bot protection). This binds the SELLER (`podatnik`, the taxpayer issuing the invoice) and is required on every invoice except two narrow, non-waiving substitutions: pkt 24 lit. a (a PL-prefixed number for one triangulation-type intra-EU case) and pkt 25 (an EX-suffixed cross-border small-business-exemption number, a 2025 addition under art. 113a ust. 1) — neither carve-out removes the requirement, both substitute a differently-formatted identifier for the same slot. There is no exemption for a small/exempt domestic seller comparable to France's or Portugal's franchise-based waiver of the identifier itself. Also confirmed NOT waived by the <=450 zl / 100 EUR simplified-invoice threshold (art. 106e ust. 5 pkt 3 i ust. 6): that threshold omits only the buyer's name/address and price-breakdown detail (pkt 3, 8, 9, 11-14), never the seller's or buyer's identification number — ust. 6 goes further and forbids using the threshold AT ALL for a sale where no buyer number under ust. 1 pkt 5 is stated, i.e. the simplification is designed for the known-buyer case, not as a blanket small-amount exemption from identification. IMPORTANT TEXTUAL POINT: the Act's own text never uses the abbreviation "NIP" anywhere in art. 106e, or (per a full-text search of the whole consolidated text) anywhere in the Act at all — it always uses the phrase quoted above. "NIP" is defined in a SEPARATE statute, ustawa z dnia 13 października 1995 r. o zasadach ewidencji i identyfikacji podatników i płatników (read as the tekst jednolity at Dz.U. 2026 poz. 151, https://dziennikustaw.gov.pl/D2026000015101.pdf, same method, 2026-09-13): its art. 3 ust. 1 assigns NIP to "pozostałych podmiotów podlegających obowiązkowi ewidencyjnemu" (all OTHER — i.e. non-natural-person — entities subject to the registration duty) but PESEL instead to a natural person who is neither a registered active VAT taxpayer nor otherwise required to register (art. 3 ust. 1 pkt 1, ust. 1a). `appliesTo` is therefore deliberately set to `'COMPANY'`, NOT `'BOTH'`: for a COMPANY-record seller, NIP specifically (not PESEL) is what this same identification Act assigns, unconditionally alongside art. 106e's own unconditional seller mandate — but for an INDIVIDUAL-record seller the correct identifier can legally be PESEL instead, a different scheme this catalog does not model at all; labelling this fact "NIP" and applying it to INDIVIDUAL sellers too would be wrong in exactly that case, not merely imprecise. `required` is nonetheless set to `false` at country level, for the SAME structural reason as Italy's own facts (see it.json's file-level notes for the full reasoning, reproduced here briefly): this catalog's `appliesTo` axis is consumed identically by the SELLER call-sites (`onboarding.tsx`/`company.settings.tsx`, always `partyType: "COMPANY"`) and the BUYER call-site (`client-upsert.tsx`, `partyType` from the client's own record type), with `required: true` enforced as a real hard save-block in all three. Poland's BUYER-side rule (art. 106e ust. 1 pkt 5) is genuinely conditional — quoted here for completeness: «5) numer, za pomocą którego nabywca towarów lub usług jest zidentyfikowany na potrzeby podatku lub podatku od wartości dodanej, pod którym otrzymał on towary lub usługi, z zastrzeżeniem pkt 24 lit. b;» — self-limiting by its own wording rather than carved out by a numbered exception: it only obligates stating the buyer's number when the buyer actually HAS one and used it to receive the supply; a private consumer simply has no such number to state, so the obligation has no object for that buyer, not because a waiver applies. This is a materially different drafting technique from Italy's (which names Codice Fiscale as an explicit alternative document) but reaches the same practical conclusion this catalog must respect: the buyer's own NIP cannot be safely marked `required: true` here either, so — exactly as for Italy — a single `required` value cannot honestly serve both the seller's unconditional duty and the buyer's conditional one, and `false` is the value that never risks refusing a lawful save. What a resolutionNote-style fix would need: a way to ask whether a given party is itself a registered VAT taxpayer (or, on the seller side, whether an INDIVIDUAL seller is VAT-registered/cash-register-using — the PESEL/NIP switch above) — the same missing axis this task's report names for Italy. No separate `unverified` fact is added for this buyer-side half, unlike Italy's Codice Fiscale: Poland has no second, distinctly-named identifier scheme to host it under (the buyer's number, when owed at all, IS the same NIP already modeled here) — the conditional buyer-side position is instead documented here, in this fact's own `notes`, and in this file's own top-level `notes` below, rather than invented as a second scheme entry with nothing new to say. REGON and KRS (art. 96b ust. 1 i ust. 3 pkt 3 i 5 — the public "wykaz podatników VAT" the tax administration publishes, a completely different provision from art. 106e) are established NOT to be invoice-content requirements at all: a full-text search of the whole consolidated Act for "REGON" and "Krajowym Rejestrze Sądowym" found zero occurrences inside art. 106e or its neighboring invoice-content articles (106a-106q) — neither is added as a scheme here on the strength of commercial habit alone.

taxSystem.notes: PROVENANCE REPLACED (2026-09-13), rate unchanged (23%): this entry used to cite the HTTP JSON response body of the European Commission's Taxes in Europe Database (TEDB, DG TAXUD) — an official but non-statutory source, consulted 2026-09-01. The repository now holds the statute itself, quoted verbatim by vat-rates/data/pl.json's own 'pl-standard' entry: Ustawa z dnia 11 marca 2004 r. o podatku od towarów i usług, art. 41 ust. 1 together with art. 146ef ust. 1 pkt 1), read live on 2026-09-13 in the tekst jednolity PDF (Dz.U. 2025 poz. 775) at https://dziennikustaw.gov.pl/DU/2025/775/D2025000077501.pdf (see that file's entry and its own notes for the full retrieval method — curl -L then pdftotext -layout, not a fetch-summary). The `sourceText` and `sourceCheckedAt` above are copied byte-for-byte from that entry, never retyped or translated. THE RATE ACTUALLY IN FORCE IS 23%, AND IT IS ART. 146EF THAT PRODUCES IT, NOT ART. 41 ALONE: art. 41 ust. 1 sets a BASE rate of 22%; art. 146ef ust. 1 pkt 1) raises it to 23% for as long as an annual conditional test tied to defence spending as a share of GDP is met — a test that vat-rates/data/pl.json's own notes record as having been met without interruption since 2024-01-01. This note must not be read as saying art. 41 by itself yields 23% — it does not, it yields 22%; the 23% actually charged today is art. 146ef overriding that 22% base, and the sourceText above quotes both provisions together for exactly that reason. Both citations (the TEDB reading and the statute) agree on the same figure (23%); nothing about the rate changed, only which source is cited — a statute a reader can check beats a reproduced JSON payload. Consumer note (unchanged from the prior citation): this table exists to unblock `documents/tax/tax-engine.ts#ossDestinationVat` (per `resolve-invoice-tax.ts`'s own header, "OSS with no destination rate table"), which reads only `dest.standardRate` — never `reducedRates` — and `DocumentLine` (`documents/tax/types.ts`) carries no per-line product category a reduced rate could even be selected against; that is why reducedRates are still deliberately not modeled here.

rule.rateDateRule: The NBP Table A average rate of the LAST BUSINESS DAY PRECEDING the day the tax obligation arises (VAT act art. 31a ust. 1), strictly BEFORE the tax point, never on it, unlike France's and Italy's own 'on or before' anchor. This codebase has no per-operation tax-point date on an invoice, so the tax point is approximated by the document's own issue date, and the rate is resolved for the last NBP-published business day strictly before that date. Poland's statute ALSO lets the taxpayer opt into the ECB rate instead (art. 31a ust. 1, same paragraph); that option is never exercised here, see `notes`.

rule.notes: Art. 106e ust. 11 names only the TAX amount ('kwoty podatku'), never the taxable base, as the figure that must be shown in złoty, hence `taxableAmountRequiredOnInvoice: false`, the same posture France's own BOFiP §380 documents for the identical distinction. Art. 31a ust. 1 lets a taxpayer choose the ECB rate INSTEAD of NBP Table A; this codebase never exercises that option: issue #517 is explicit that Poland's rate source must be NBP Table A specifically, 'or a clear refusal when no NBP rate is available; never silently use another source', see `../nbp-rates-client.ts`'s own header for the refusal this rule drives. facts.notes: RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-28 (issue #527) against the Ministry of Finance's own tax explanatory note ("Objaśnienia podatkowe", 28 January 2026, art. 14a par. 1 pkt 2 Ordynacja podatkowa, gov.pl/attachment/8fde481a-18aa-4b1b-843e-5bbd303d6f94 - fetched and read directly): every claim below is CONFIRMED, word for word, including the 2024 turnover reference year for the 200 000 000 zl threshold (a couple of low-quality secondary summaries say "2025" - wrong, contradicted by the MoF's own text and by the statute mirrors on lexlege.pl/arslege.pl, which all agree on 2024). The MoF note itself states plainly this regime applies "od dnia 1 lutego 2026 r." with no slippage. As of this re-check, BOTH real-world start dates have already passed: the >200M zl tier has been bound since 1 February 2026, and the general tier since 1 April 2026 (corroborated by an individual tax ruling applying KSeF post-go-live, Dyrektor KIS 9 April 2026, sygn. 0114-KDIP1-1.4012.132.2026.1.ESZ). THIS DOES NOT CHANGE THE CONCLUSION BELOW: the art. 145m ust. 1 monthly allowance (<= 10 000 zl of structured-eligible sales per calendar month) remains ACTIVE through 31 December 2026 for every obligated taxpayer, general tier included - so even a company well past its own go-live date can still lawfully send a plain invoice for a given month under that threshold. Arming `requirement: 'mandated'` today would refuse those still-lawful invoices exactly as before; the reasoning that keeps this fact `suggested` (see below) is therefore UNCHANGED by both go-live dates now being in the past, not weakened by it. One adjacent, NOT settled, development found in Polish tax press (rp.pl, bezprawnik.pl, mid-to-late September 2026): the Ministry of Finance is reported to be proposing to defer PENALTIES for KSeF errors from 1 January 2027 to 1 January 2028 - about the SANCTION regime, never the invoicing-obligation dates themselves, and not confirmed via any primary gov.pl page as enacted (could be a draft nowelizacja still) - noted here for completeness, not acted on. Base obligation (art. 106ga ust. 1 of the VAT act of 11 March 2004, unified text announced by the Marszałek Sejmu on 21 May 2025, Dz.U. 2025 poz. 775): this is the citation carried by `sourceText` above. The same article, ust. 2, provides SIX exemption categories from this obligation, reproduced here verbatim because they condition who is even concerned by KSeF: « 2. Obowiązek, o którym mowa w ust. 1, nie dotyczy wystawiania faktur: 1) przez podatnika nieposiadającego siedziby działalności gospodarczej ani stałego miejsca prowadzenia działalności gospodarczej na terytorium kraju; 2) przez podatnika nieposiadającego siedziby działalności gospodarczej na terytorium kraju, który posiada stałe miejsce prowadzenia działalności gospodarczej na terytorium kraju, przy czym to stałe miejsce prowadzenia działalności nie uczestniczy w dostawie towarów lub świadczeniu usług, dla których wystawiono fakturę; 3) przez podatnika korzystającego z procedur szczególnych, o których mowa w dziale XII w rozdziałach 7, 7a i 9, dokumentujących czynności rozliczane w tych procedurach; 4) na rzecz nabywcy towarów lub usług będącego osobą fizyczną nieprowadzącą działalności gospodarczej; 5) w przypadku odpowiednio udokumentowanych dostaw towarów lub świadczenia usług, określonych w przepisach wydanych na podstawie art. 106s; 6) przez podatnika korzystającego ze zwolnienia, o którym mowa w art. 113a ust. 1. » The base date often cited (1 February 2026) is that of art. 23 of the law of 16 June 2023 (Dz.U. 2023 poz. 1598, as amended), printed in the same unified text: « Art. 23. Ustawa wchodzi w życie z dniem 1 lutego 2026 r., z wyjątkiem: 1) art. 3 pkt 1, 3 i pkt 5 [...], które wchodzą w życie z dniem następującym po dniu ogłoszenia; 2) art. 1 pkt 8, 9, 10 i 14 oraz art. 14, które wchodzą w życie z dniem 1 września 2023 r.; 3) art. 1 pkt 4 i 5, art. 4–6, art. 7 pkt 1 i 3, art. 9 i art. 18–21, które wchodzą w życie z dniem 1 stycznia 2024 r.; 4) art. 1 pkt 7 lit. e, pkt 13 lit. b w zakresie art. 106h ust. 2 i 4, pkt 24 w zakresie art. 106ni ust. 1–3 i 5–7 i pkt 30, które wchodzą w życie z dniem 1 sierpnia 2026 r. » BUT two transitional articles — inserted by a MORE RECENT law, that of 5 August 2025 (Dz.U. 2025 poz. 1203, art. 1 pkt 34, published 1 September 2025) — replace an older transitional regime (the same unified text of May 2025 still carried, before this August law, an art. 145l running only until 31 July 2026 and no art. 145m — an OUTDATED version, no longer to be cited) and change the real scope of this date for most taxpayers: « „Art. 145l. W okresie od dnia 1 lutego 2026 r. do dnia 31 marca 2026 r. podatnicy obowiązani do wystawiania faktur ustrukturyzowanych mogą wystawiać faktury elektroniczne lub faktury w postaci papierowej, jeżeli łączna wartość sprzedaży wraz z kwotą podatku u tych podatników nie przekroczyła w 2024 r. kwoty 200 000 000 zł. Art. 145m. 1. W okresie od dnia 1 kwietnia 2026 r. do dnia 31 grudnia 2026 r. podatnicy obowiązani do wystawiania faktur ustrukturyzowanych mogą wystawiać faktury elektroniczne lub faktury w postaci papierowej, jeżeli łączna wartość sprzedaży wraz z kwotą podatku u tych podatników udokumentowana tymi fakturami wystawionymi w danym miesiącu jest mniejsza lub równa 10 000 zł. 2. Podatnik, o którym mowa w ust. 1, traci prawo do wystawiania faktur elektronicznych oraz faktur w postaci papierowej począwszy od faktury, którą przekroczono wartość, o której mowa w ust. 1.” » In other words, as of the drafting date (2026-09-13): taxpayers whose 2024 turnover including VAT exceeded 200,000,000 zł are indeed bound from 1 February 2026 (no grace period, art. 145l); ALL OTHER taxpayers subject to the obligation remain free to issue ordinary invoices (electronic or paper) up to and including 31 March 2026 — they are therefore only bound from 1 April 2026; and, independently of this threshold, EVERY taxpayer subject to the obligation keeps, until 31 December 2026, the right to issue ordinary invoices for a given calendar month as long as the total including VAT of sales documented by structured invoices that month stays ≤ 10,000 zł — losing this grace period from the invoice that exceeds this threshold onward (art. 145m ust. 1 and 2). This entry deliberately stays `requirement: 'suggested'` despite provenance now being `legal`: `channel-policy/mandate.ts#activeChannelMandateFor` only knows a SINGLE `mandatedFrom` date, compared against each invoice's own `issueDate` — it knows nothing of the company's 2024 turnover nor of its structured-eligible sales for the current month. Arming this fact with `mandatedFrom: '2026-02-01'` (or even '2026-04-01') WOULD REFUSE invoices that are still perfectly lawful: an electronic or paper invoice issued by an SME under the 200,000,000 zł threshold before 1 April 2026, or by ANY taxpayer for a month where its structured-eligible sales stay ≤ 10,000 zł until 31 December 2026 inclusive, remains LAWFUL today. Refusing a still-lawful invoice would be a PRODUCT FAILURE; leaving this fact `suggested` is only a GAP that the user remains free to avoid by connecting KSeF voluntarily — the former is worse than the latter. A correct implementation would require (1) that the mandate mechanism know the company's 2024 turnover including VAT, to decide between 1 February and 1 April 2026 (art. 145l), and (2) that it know its structured-eligible sales FOR THE CALENDAR MONTH of each invoice, to apply or not the art. 145m allowance until 31 December 2026 — two pieces of data this product neither computes nor stores today (they would need to be derived from the company's own invoice history, or explicitly declared), and a mandate schema that accepts more than a single date (an annual turnover threshold, a rolling monthly cap) to faithfully represent this two-speed timetable plus its residual allowance.

rules.label: VAT
rules.legalRef: ustawa o VAT art. 112, renvoi vers Ordynacja podatkowa art. 70 § 1
rules.notes: Raw text retrieved on 2026-09-13. Ustawa o VAT (consolidated text, Dz.U. 2024 poz. 361) via curl -sL https://dziennikustaw.gov.pl/DU/2024/361/D2024000036101.pdf (HTTP 200) then pdftotext -layout. Art. 112: « Podatnicy są obowiązani przechowywać ewidencje prowadzone dla celów rozliczania podatku oraz wszystkie dokumenty, w szczególności faktury, związane z tym rozliczaniem do czasu upływu terminu przedawnienia zobowiązania podatkowego, z zastrzeżeniem art. 109b ust. 7, art. 130d ust. 3, art. 134 ust. 3, art. 138h ust. 3 i art. 138i ust. 8. » (the referenced carve-outs — art. 109b/130d/134/138h/138i — are OSS/IOSS/import special regimes, not relevant to an ordinary domestic invoice). This article does NOT set a number of years: it refers to the LIMITATION period of the tax obligation itself. Ordynacja podatkowa (consolidated text, Dz.U. 2026 poz. 622, the Marshal's consolidation of 22 April 2026) via curl -sL https://api.sejm.gov.pl/eli/acts/DU/2026/622/text.pdf (HTTP 200; isap.sejm.gov.pl sits behind Incapsula and was avoided) then pdftotext -layout. Art. 70 § 1: « Zobowiązanie podatkowe przedawnia się z upływem 5 lat, licząc od końca roku kalendarzowego, w którym upłynął termin płatności podatku. » — FIVE years, counted from the end of the calendar year in which the tax PAYMENT deadline fell — not the year the invoice was issued. Poland's VAT payment deadline falls the month (or quarter, for a quarterly filer) after the invoice's own period: an invoice issued near year-end can therefore have its payment deadline — and hence the starting point of the 5 years — fall in January of the FOLLOWING year. Neither a company's VAT filing frequency (monthly/quarterly) nor its exact settlement periods are stored by this product: the exact deadline year therefore cannot be determined from the document alone. SAFE reading adopted (never the shortest one): origin `taxDeadlineYearEndUnknownSafe` = 31 December of (year of issuance + 1), which covers both filing regimes without needing to know which applies — see compute-retention.ts for the demonstration that this ceiling can never be exceeded by the true deadline. Data that would make this point exact: the company's VAT filing frequency and the actual settlement date of the relevant period.

retention.notes: A single text, but two distinct articles, and a period that is NOT anchored on the issuance date: see the rule's own note above for the full chain (ustawa o VAT art. 112 → Ordynacja podatkowa art. 70 § 1) and why the safe origin adopted deliberately differs from `issueDateYearEnd`. Established on 2026-09-13 with the coordinator's help (access via `api.sejm.gov.pl`, which bypasses `isap.sejm.gov.pl`'s Incapsula wall); every citation was re-checked by grep against its own retrieval before this file was written, per this module's own discipline.

field.label: Correction reason
field.helpText: Why this invoice corrects the one above ("przyczyna korekty") — carried onto the KSeF submission as FA(3)'s own PrzyczynaKorekty element (formats/national/fa3-provider.ts) once a corrected invoice is set.

field.label: Supply type
field.helpText: Whether this line is a delivery of goods or a supply of services — it decides how a cross-border sale is taxed. Goods sold to a consumer in another EU member state are an intra-Community distance sale, taxed where they arrive once your EU-wide distance sales pass EUR 10 000 in a calendar year (Directive 2006/112/EC art. 33(a) and art. 59c); the same sale as a service stays taxable here (art. 45). Optional: a line that declares nothing is treated as a supply of services.

countryFields.notes: Poland's own field overlay — a SINGLE addition, `correctionReason`, conditionally required (`requiredIfPresent: "correctsInvoiceId"` — descriptors/types.ts) rather than unconditionally: `correctsInvoiceId` (invoice.descriptor.ts trunk field) is what actually flags an invoice as a correction, so an ORDINARY Polish invoice (the overwhelming majority) never has to carry a reason at all — only once `correctsInvoiceId` is set does this field become mandatory on THIS screen. IMPORTANT PROVENANCE NUANCE, read before assuming this is a legal citation: the reason is legally OPTIONAL, not mandatory. Art. 106j ust. 2 (the faktura korygująca's own MANDATORY content list) does not list a reason at all — verbatim: "2. Faktura korygująca powinna zawierać: ... 2a) numer identyfikujący w Krajowym Systemie e-Faktur fakturę, której dotyczy faktura korygująca ...; 3) dane zawarte w fakturze ...; 5) jeżeli korekta wpływa na zmianę podstawy opodatkowania lub kwoty podatku należnego – odpowiednio kwotę korekty ...; 6) w przypadkach innych niż wskazane w pkt 5 – prawidłową treść korygowanych pozycji." The reason lives ONE paragraph down, in the file's own OPTIONAL list: "2a. Faktura korygująca może zawierać: 1) wyrazy \"FAKTURA KORYGUJĄCA\" albo \"KOREKTA\"; 2) przyczynę korekty." ("może" = may/can, not "powinna"/"musi") — ustawa o VAT z 11 marca 2004 r., tekst jednolity Dz.U. 2025 poz. 775, art. 106j ust. 2 i 2a (isap.sejm.gov.pl, checked 2026-09-16, raw consolidated text — same source correction-routes/data/pl.json's own AUTHORITY_ANNULMENT citation already reads). Requiring it here is therefore a PRODUCT decision (a correction naming no reason at all is a poor audit trail, and the Ministry's own FA(3) schema still exposes PrzyczynaKorekty as an element worth filling even though the underlying statute never forces it), not a legal `kind: 'legal'`-grade fact the way `correction-routes/data/pl.json`'s own CORRECTIVE_INVOICE route citation is — this file's own schema (`country-fields/schema.ts`) does not require field-overlay operations to carry provenance at all (see that file's own header: 'add/modify/remove this field' is a structural/product fact, not itself a new legal claim), which is exactly the case here. The FIELD's own server-side enforcement (never trusted from the screen alone) needs NO bespoke code at all: `requiredIfPresent` is read generically by `descriptors/validate.ts#validateAgainstDescriptor`, which `documents.service.ts#runAction` already runs, against the MERGED descriptor, for every action on this type (save-draft included) — a Polish invoice with `correctsInvoiceId` set and no `correctionReason` is refused (400, naming the field) before any handler ever sees it, proven end to end by `43-correction-routes.cy.ts`'s own Poland describe block. SECOND OPERATION, added later: the SAME `supplyType` line subfield France's own `fr.json` already adds, byte-identical in key, kind, label, options and optionality — a LINE subfield, unlike `correctionReason` above. WHY THE FIELD IS IDENTICAL IN ALL FIVE COUNTRIES RATHER THAN A PER-COUNTRY VARIANT: what reads it — `tax/resolve-invoice-tax.ts`, feeding `tax/tax-engine.ts#determineLineTax` — branches on the goods/services distinction of Directive 2006/112/EC (arts. 32, 33(a) and 59c for an intra-Community distance sale of goods, art. 45 for a service), which binds every member state identically; the same reasoning `tax/types.ts`'s own `DistanceSalesRegime` states for art. 59c ('art. 59c applies identically in all of them'). Poland's transposition defines the two in the directive's own terms — « Przez dostawę towarów, o której mowa w art. 5 ust. 1 pkt 1, rozumie się przeniesienie prawa do rozporządzania towarami jak właściciel » (ustawa o VAT, art. 7 ust. 1) against « Przez świadczenie usług, o którym mowa w art. 5 ust. 1 pkt 1, rozumie się każde świadczenie na rzecz osoby fizycznej, osoby prawnej lub jednostki organizacyjnej niemającej osobowości prawnej, które nie stanowi dostawy towarów w rozumieniu art. 7 » (same act, art. 8 ust. 1), the residual definition the directive itself uses. Same consolidated text this file's own art. 106j citation above already reads — ustawa z 11 marca 2004 r. o podatku od towarów i usług, tekst jednolity Dz.U. 2025 poz. 775 — but fetched from a DIFFERENT host on 2026-09-21: isap.sejm.gov.pl now answers an automated request with an Incapsula challenge page rather than the PDF, so the text was read from the Dziennik Ustaw itself (https://dziennikustaw.gov.pl/D2025000077501.pdf), the same obwieszczenie. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT MIRRORED FROM FRANCE: the French overlay's own `helpText` names BT-23 (« cadre de facturation »), which is a FRENCH obligation — `formats/semantic/business-process.ts#resolveFrenchBusinessProcessCode` derives that code only for a seller whose country has an active BT-23 rule in `content-requirements/`, and France is the only country with one — so a Polish seller declaring a supply type changes the exported document not at all; it changes the TAX determination, which is what this operation's own help text names instead. NO RETROACTIVE EFFECT ON STORED DOCUMENTS: the field is OPTIONAL and nothing back-fills it. `resolve-invoice-tax.ts` narrows a line's raw `supplyType` to GOODS/SERVICES and treats anything else — including absent — as SERVICES, emitting a named warning; that fallback is untouched here, so every invoice stored before this operation existed resolves exactly as it did before, and only a line a user explicitly marks as goods reaches the distance-sales branch. DIGITAL IS NOT OFFERED, on purpose: `tax/types.ts`'s own `SupplyType` has a third value, but `resolve-invoice-tax.ts` narrows a stored value to GOODS/SERVICES only, so a 'DIGITAL' option would be silently discarded on the way in — offering it would need that narrowing widened first, for all five countries including France.

requiredClientIdentifiers.label: NIP (Numer Identyfikacji Podatkowej)
requiredClientIdentifiers.why: FA(3) requires the buyer's NIP in the Podmiot2/DaneIdentyfikacyjne block (`formats/national/fa3-provider.ts` reads `getIdentifier(client, 'VAT')`, stripped of any leading two-letter country prefix) — a government client (a Jednostki Samorządu Terytorialnego/JST or a central body) with no NIP on file cannot be built into a FA(3) document at all. ksef.podatki.gov.pl's own JST page confirms this is not a formality: "Podatnicy krajowi posiadający NIP, odbierają faktury przy użyciu systemu (czyli elektronicznie)" ("Domestic taxpayers WITH a NIP receive invoices using the system [KSeF], i.e. electronically") — the NIP is what makes a Polish public body a KSeF-addressable recipient at all.

provenance.sourceText: eInvoicing Country Factsheet — Poland (European Commission, Digital Building Blocks, eInvoicing space, page last updated 14 Aug 2025): "Businesses will use KSeF for B2B e-Invoices, while B2G transactions can be processed through either KSeF or PEF" — both platforms operate "within the OpenPeppol network". Separately, on the Polish Ministry of Finance's own KSeF portal (ksef.podatki.gov.pl/jednostki-samorzadu-terytorialnego-jst/, the page dedicated to local government units): "Podatnicy krajowi posiadający NIP, odbierają faktury przy użyciu systemu (czyli elektronicznie)" — domestic NIP-holding taxpayers, which includes JST public bodies, receive their invoices through KSeF. The same official page lists the phased mandatory rollout: "1 lutego 2026", "1 kwietnia 2026" (with a 10,000 PLN/month threshold exemption), the transitional period for certain exemptions (simplified invoices, cash-register receipts) ending "31 grudnia 2026", and full mandatory compliance from "1 stycznia 2027".

b2gRouting.notes: READ DIRECTLY on 2026-09-02, TWO CONVERGING SOURCES: (1) ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/spaces/DIGITAL/pages/467108896/eInvoicing+in+Poland (the European Commission's own official country factsheet); (2) ksef.podatki.gov.pl (the Polish Ministry of Finance's own KSeF portal), in particular its page dedicated to local government units (JST), ksef.podatki.gov.pl/jednostki-samorzadu-terytorialnego-jst/ — reached after two HTTP 301 redirects (podatki.gov.pl/ksef/ → podatki.gov.pl/ksef → ksef.podatki.gov.pl), all followed and read, never guessed. DECISION ON THE CHANNEL — SETTLED BY READING, NOT BY THE MOST OBVIOUS OPTION: the Commission's factsheet documents TWO possible Polish B2G channels, KSeF AND PEF (Platforma Elektronicznego Fakturowania) — PEF having "adopted the Peppol BIS standard and incorporated Polish-specific requirements" then "developed additional extensions to the e-Invoicing standard... approved by OpenPeppol". This rule deliberately chooses KSeF, NOT PEF/Peppol, for a reason of REAL DELIVERABILITY, not preference: PEF's Polish extension (the CIUS/Poland-specific Peppol extensions, approved by OpenPeppol but specific to it) is NOT vendored in this repository — no `formats/*-provider.ts` builds it — whereas KSeF AND its national FA(3) format (`formats/national/fa3-provider.ts`, judged against the official vendored XSD `vendored/pl/schemat_FA3.xsd`, never against an unsuited generic EN 16931 Schematron) are ALREADY implemented and PROVEN LIVE (see the session's own memory: "KSeF channel proven end-to-end, real CLEARED + ksefNumber, 2026-06-28") — sending generic Peppol BIS to PEF would contradict the rule as read (PEF requires the Polish-specific extensions, never bare Peppol BIS), exactly the case this task's own instructions ask to avoid; KSeF, conversely, IS a channel the same factsheet states is usable for B2G ("B2G transactions can be processed through either KSeF or PEF"), and its FA(3) format is the Polish national format itself, never a generic substitute. `transportId: "ksef"` and `formatSyntax: "fa3"` therefore reference building blocks that ACTUALLY exist and are already proven, not a bet. DISTINCTION FROM `channel-policy/data/pl.json` (pre-existing, not modified by this task): that file encodes a DIFFERENT axis — the mandate for the Polish SELLER's OWN country, for EVERY invoice it issues (`requirement: "suggested"`, provenance `unverified`, for lack of as clean a citation as this one at the time); THIS rule encodes the B2G axis — the government CLIENT's country, regardless of the seller's own country — and carries ITS OWN `legal` provenance, independently sourced today (two direct readings, never carried over from channel-policy/pl.json's own note, which itself remains unverified by this task). HONEST LIMIT ON THE TIMELINE: as of the reading date (2026-09-02), KSeF's mandatory rollout is under way but NOT COMPLETE (milestones read: 1 February 2026, 1 April 2026 with an exemption under 10,000 PLN/month, the transitional period for certain exemptions ending 31 December 2026, full compliance from 1 January 2027) — this rule asserts that KSeF IS the recognized Polish B2G channel, never that EVERY send through it is today legally forced for EVERY company size; unlike `channel-policy/schema.ts`, the `b2g-routing/schema.ts` format in any case has NO temporal field (`mandatedFrom`) to grade this — see `schema.ts`'s own header, a B2G rule is a single rule, not dated. NO `requiredDocumentFields` is added: FA(3) carries no B2G-specific field requirement beyond the NIP already covered by `requiredClientIdentifiers` above.
